To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of reasoning in cases can be naturally incorporated into a framework that uses derived antecedents to represent and reason with incomplete information, and (2), the use of reasoning about cases can be naturally and efficiently incorporated into a theorem prover.
reasoning by cases can and should be done in the framework of conditional programs.

(a) a goal can be analyzed into cases based on the context in which it occurs; (b) reasoning by cases can proceed in parallel with reasoning by rules; (c) the conditional programs resulting from reasoning by cases are formed in a natural and intuitive manner; (d) the conditional programs are formed in such a way that they can be used to reason by cases in a subsequent derivation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How can reasoning by cases be naturally and automatically accomplished in the context of derived antecedent reasoning?
the problem of how to reason by cases when needed, and how to combine the results of the reasoning by cases into a single deduction.

the following issues: (1) How to determine when reasoning by cases should be used; (2) how a goal can be decomposed into cases; (3) how the deduction is carried out in each case and how the results are combined; (4) how the results of reasoning by cases can then be used in the deduction.

the paper provides an account of reasoning by cases in the context of a particular formalism (Smith 1983).

we have developed a system for reasoning by cases that can be naturally applied when reasoning about the existence of solutions to equations and inequations, and for which the resulting conditional programs can be used to solve problems in a variety of domains.
the use of reasoning-by-cases in this framework is natural, efficient, and effective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reasoning by cases is a natural and effective feature of a logic programming system that is based on a logic with derived antecedents.
we have shown how reasoning by cases and the formation of conditional programs are two sides of the same coin, and how they are naturally accomplished in the derived-antecedents framework.
we have developed an elegant and efficient method for carrying out case-based reasoning in the context of a general deductive system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of derived antecedent rules can provide a natural framework in which to perform reasoning by cases and form conditional programs.
reasoning by cases is an integral part of the process of reasoning with conditional knowledge.
the use of derived antecedent rules, together with the context of a goal, provides a natural and powerful mechanism for reasoning by cases.
